summary.prose: Build the saved-connection foundation so users can create and edit connections without exposing stored credentials or losing track of whether a save succeeded. Add safe retries, conflict checks and protection for connections in use, plus the memory-only file execution foundation needed by later temporary-connection work. Enable writes only after driver coverage, recovery, compatibility and deployment filesystem checks pass; the manager UI and temporary sessions follow in separate stories.

tasks.title: Classify every supported driver's editable and secret fields
tasks.summary: Inspect actual driver/config/converter reads and persist a per-kind matrix with public editable fields, credential slots, retained-only fields and rejected legacy shapes, including recursive/partitioning and all supported options. This is a design-input task; do not implement projection/materialization until it has no unclassified fields.
acceptanceChecks: Every runtime listRegisteredKinds entry maps to a source-backed row and fixture; unknown secret-bearing fields fail closed.
Pinned-family and URL/path dialect compatibility is explicit; matrix is a reviewed build input, not a family-wide secrecy assumption.
Revalidate current-source import/alias/factory and registered-kind inventory before implementation; changed design assumptions require back-flow, not silent contract changes.

tests.name: CM-S1-J: legacy success shapes versus v2 structured errors; malformed requests, unknown ticket fields, wrong root/target and no stored-secret return.

Unknown supported fields survive label-only edit; identity/kind/family changes reject; cancellation before mutate changes zero bytes/keys.
Explicit legacy pinned family remains effective or is safely read-only, never normalized.

acceptanceChecks: Legacy same-UID writeFile after the new digest check gets EACCES and cannot strip envelope; old fd affects detached inode only.
Direct managed saveConnections without gate proof fails; no chmod-to-writable live path.
Uncertain rename/fsync is recoverable rather than presumed rejected; unsupported/privileged permission semantics disable adoption.
